literal: Those who possess knowledge everything they possess; those without knowledge whatever they possess even if, they are without.
translation: Those who possess wisdom possess everything. Those without wisdom possess nothing, no matter what else they may have.
modern: அறிவுடையவர்கள் உலகத்தில் உள்ள எல்லாவற்றையும் பெற்றவர்கள் ஆவார்கள். அறிவு இல்லாதவர்கள் வேறு எதைப் பெற்றிருந்தாலும், உண்மையில் ஒன்றும் இல்லாதவர்களே ஆவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the true value of wisdom with material possessions. The word 'அறிவுடையார்' refers to those who have acquired true knowledge, and the poet declares that they effectively possess everything. Conversely, 'அறிவிலார்' are those lacking wisdom; even if they own vast wealth or other worldly goods ('என் உடையரேனும்'), they are considered to have nothing ('இலர்'). The underlying message is that knowledge is the only complete and secure possession, rendering all other acquisitions meaningless without it.
